intended_object: The subgroup T_n of GL_n(R) made up of invertible upper-triangular matrices (Milne, item 2.9), over a commutative ring R. Here the index set is any finite linearly ordered type ι. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The carrier is the set of g in `GL ι R` whose underlying matrix satisfies `Matrix.IsUpperTriangular`. Mathlib defines `IsUpperTriangular` as `BlockTriangular M id`, which means M i j = 0 whenever j < i. That is the standard upper-triangular condition.

The three closure properties are proved correctly:
- the identity matrix is upper triangular;
- a product of upper-triangular matrices is upper triangular;
- the inverse of an invertible block-triangular matrix is block-triangular. This uses Mathlib's `blockTriangular_inv_of_blockTriangular`, which needs `CommRing`.

So the subgroup is exactly the group of invertible upper-triangular matrices. Over a commutative ring, these are the upper-triangular matrices whose diagonal entries are units, which matches T_n.

The generality is natural:
- any commutative ring R, which is what the inverse lemma needs;
- any finite linearly ordered index type, with `Fin n` as the special case.

The only artificial restriction is that ι and R must live in the same universe `u`. This is a minor technical restriction, not a mathematical one.

I searched Mathlib for an existing upper-triangular (Borel) subgroup of `GeneralLinearGroup` and found none. Mathlib only has the predicate `Matrix.IsUpperTriangular` and lemmas about it.
